Lady Julia's African Adventure - A Success

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
When we waved Lady Albu of on her African adventure adventure in June last year we hoped she and her indescribably tiny 1997 Toyota Conquest would make the drive up Africa from Cape Town to Alexandria, Egypt but in our heart of hearts we were not totally confident. We applauded her spirit. At 80 years old Julia and her car Tracy, 20 years old makes brave millennials look terrifyingly tame.

But Julia and Tracy – newly upholstered in bright pink roses – on the 8th January after a day’s driving through a horrendous sandstorm were, finally, able to see the glistening waters of the Med on Alexandria’s shores.


Further information:
It’s been a hectic six months. We will relive just some of the adventures Julia has had as she drove up Africa, sometimes with friends or family accompanying…sometimes a new friend made as she charmed her way through each country. The beds she was offered from strangers or through people following her on social media and wanted to be part of this tantalizing adventure.

From a baby elephant Julia adopted from Dr Dame Daphne Sheldrick at her elephant sanctuary in Kenya …travelling through Ethiopia visiting Axum, Lalibela, the ancient churches, staying in the monasteries. Driving upwards and onwards through the sensational Simean Mountains.

In Sudan, picking up a hitchhiker, being raided by the police fighting back when the official started drinking her Blue Nile Water. Driving through the sandstorms of the Sudan and sleeping under the Meroe Pyramids.

Christmas spent in the Nubian desert, their festive lunch at the home of new found friend Magzoub (who drives a 1947 Morris Minor – instant bonding for Julia) consisted of fresh fish just caught from the Nile . freshly baked bread, chili paste and rocket grown from his organic vegetable garden on the banks of the Nile…a feast of delight in Julia words.

Finally reaching Egypt - after a paper trail of epic proportions to get carnets and permissions, stamped sealed – is entered, Abu Simbel on shore of Lake Nasser, Luxor.. Valley of the Kings and Queens and finally Alexandria..the jackpot, Julia reached her destination on the 8th January.

It is an amazing achievement for Julia to have travelled this journey and throughout it all she has had countless followers advising her, being inspired by her intrepid spirit and offering all sorts of help when she was in some desperate straits. Julia’s own very special brand of charm and open heartedness has made this journey a delight to be part of.

Press Release:



Lady Julia Albu’s African Adventure II
In June last year, Carte Blanche waved farewell to 80-year-old Julia Albu as she embarked on the ultimate adventure – a trip from Cape Town to Egypt in her 1997 Toyota Conquest. It’s been a tough 7 months but she’s made it and so has her beloved car Tracy. Carte Blanche catches up with Lady Julia who relives her remarkable experiences from facing sandstorms in Sudan to spending Christmas in the Nubian desert


Script:


Julia: We had got to this marvelous camp and the next morning the light was so wonderful. I walked outside almost in a daze and their coming towards me galloping was this a snow white camel with a man on top he could have been Lawrence of Arabia the camel went down on my knees and he with such grace dismounted and offered me a seat on his camel…well I didn’t think twice in a daze got on the camel

V/O 12 sec
No this is not a romantic fantasy but one of Julia Albu’s many encounters on her epic journey across Africa…. It all started back in June last year…

Link
When you get an 80 year old woman talking about driving all the way from the Cape to Cairo in a 20 year old car with more than 300 000 km on the the clock it may be difficult to take her seriously.

Julia “ You know I believe a car has a soul and she has been with me for 20 years.”

Link
But at least some people took Julia seriously and she got a rousing send off from Gauteng…with a cavalcade of Harley Davidson riders.

V/O
Julia left her home in Jakkalsfontein on her 80th Birthday, in June last year…. After her send off in Johannesburg she headed up through Botswana, Zimbabwe Zambia.. around Lake Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, finally reaching Alexandria, Egypt on the 7th January.

Derek: Welcome back
Julia: Thank you very very much
Derek: How has your impression of Africa changed?
Julia: I am besotted about the continent there is nothing to be afraid of there is only hospitality and warmth.

Derek: Where you regarded as something as a curiosity?
Julia: No Tracy was
Derek: Tracy more than you.

V/O 16 sec
Tracy, Julia’s car, was the real reason for this African Adventure. After hearing a radio interview on the cost of Zuma’s wives cars she phoned in furious….the next thing she knew she was planning a trip in her 1997 Toyota Conquest.

Derek: What problems did you have with Tracy over this whole trip?
Julia: One problem where the starter motor didn’t work so we stopped in a little place it was in Tanzania and literally in a cupboard was a man working and he took the top of a coke tin and he beat and and cut it and he repaired Tracy and its still in there today.
Derek: With a coke tin

Derek: How many sets of tyres did you go through?
Julia: didn’t go through any
Derek: One set of tyres?
Derek: What brand were they?
Julia: I don’t know which set of tyres but they must have been very good and given to me by most divine man called Mike Kingston.

V/O
From Malawi, Julia drove into Tanzania, to Bagamoya the place from where 1000 and 1000 ‘s of slaves were shipped from Africa.

Julia: That has got the most sad dreadful that was the last hold of slaves before the slaves were shipped to .. and you know its got a feeling very sad

Link
Although family and friends joined Julia on her bucket list adventure it was followers on social media who kept her going and in turn she’s inspired many by her novel and brave journey.

Derek: Julia apart from the people you have met along the way you have inspired a lot of people through your blog and social media.
Julia: I have received messages from people I have never heard of and they have been inspirational they have pushed me when you felt Oh No they pushed me.

V/O
And Julia’s passion - collecting water – not just any water but Nile Water.
In fact she made a detour into Uganda to collect water at the source of the Nile

Julia: It’s dropped you see it’s come down,
The Blue Nile these are from Lake Tana I was lucky enough to get two.
Derek: Are these the same vintage then?
Julia: Yes exactly One is from the waterfall the Blue Waterfall and one is from Lake Tana.
Julia: This one is Murky one this is when the 2 Niles join in the Sudan.
Derek: So is this good drinking water?
Julia: No you can’t drink any of it

V/O 4 sec
In Kenya, Julia visited Daphne Sheldrick’s Elephant Orphanage

Julia: …. and what did I do I bought me an elephant.
Derek: On special?
Julia: It was on sale because it had a wobbly leg.

Julia: I had to do a U Turn when I was going into Ethiopia because I was told I cold get my visa at the border and and I cried hopelessly millions of tears so bad that the customs official said you come and sit with me and he cooked me breakfast…such a good recipe I even have the recipe.
Derek: Now this does not happen at Heathrow or anywhere else.
…never known anything like it.

V/O
Christmas was spent in the middle of the Sudan Desert, hospitality care of the kindness of strangers and it was here Tracy paired up with a new friend.

Julia: Where we were staying there is a little Morris and I said to its owner I said how old is your car and he said 72 years old, we parked the two together and I was quiet sure they had stories to tell each other, Tracy became a friend a travelling companion.
Derek: Wonderful interior still in good condition?
Julia: Looking marvelous she could to with a vacuum.

V/O
Julia’s petrol was sponsored by Carl de Beer a friend of Julia’s who couldn’t travel because he had colon cancer but wanted to be with her in spirit.

Link
The saddest part of Julia’s journey was getting the news that Carl had passed away it was Carl who had told her live your dreams while you still can

Julia: I was really devastated he so generously gave me money towards my petrol Derek: It was Carl who said live your dream while you still can.
Julia: Absolutely and never wait and always take an opportunity I couldn’t agree more with him.

V/O 10 sec
Early this year …after a mountain of paperwork due to one carnet too short they entered Egypt…by the 7th January they had reached Alexandria.

Julia: Well I was so excited to see Egypt.. I think when I hit Alexandria that was now the end I was very weepy,

V/O
Julia’s back but her odyssey is not over…Tracy is being shipped across the Med to Greece where the second part of her adventure will take place going through Europe…until she reaches London

Derek: Julia this must be one of the greatest things you have done in your life
Julia: It is and you know now that I have done it and met the people I would like to do a U
Derek: And come all the way back with Tracy?
Julia: Well ho else am I going to get Tracy back
Derek: Not in a taxi
Julia No and any body who wants to come well here is an opportunity come and drive with me and enjoy what I have been able to do …
